fields.mechanism: Infrared-based sensing to detect changes in tubing content (air vs. fluid) triggering automatic mechanical occlusion.
fields.intervention: Retrofit an infrared emitter-detector pair onto the existing disposable tubing path of the infusion pump to monitor refractive index changes indicative of flow stagnation or pressure-induced tubing deformation, coupled with a low-cost solenoid pinch valve to mechanically occlude the line upon signal threshold breach.
fields.expected_effect: Detection of flow anomalies leading to occlusion conditions at least ten minutes prior to pressure-based alarm activation by sensing fluid state changes before significant pressure buildup, while maintaining the sterile disposable path and reducing false alarms via continuous optical verification.
fields.falsification_test: Operate the retrofitted system with a controlled downstream occlusion simulated by a precision valve; verify that the infrared sensor triggers the mechanical occluder more than ten minutes before the original pump's pressure alarm activates across 50 trials with varying fluid viscosities and tubing materials.
fields.mechanism_source_span: The device employs an infrared-based sensing approach to continuously monitor tubing for the presence of air and for conditions consistent with end of infusion, such as depletion of the fluid source.
